Fundamental Delivery, Valuation & Weight Consistency

Culture Analytics Dashboard — follow-up to the three-variant backtest study. All quartile memberships are frozen from the stored Variant-W run (43 snapshots, 2015-12-31 → 2026-06-30); analyses (i) and (ii) change only the outcome variable measured on those fixed portfolios. Generated 2026-07-27.

Headline. The evidence supports the valuation-compression story with a regime-shift twist. (1) Strong-culture (Q1) companies kept delivering better fundamentals after 2021 — the Q1−Q4 median forward EPS-growth spread widened from +1.1pp to +3.4pp — while the price-return spread fell from +7.9pp pa to −0.9pp pa. (2) Q1 de-rated relative to Q4: post-2021 Q1 combined ~15% pa earnings growth with −3.3% pa re-rating. Q1's P/E premium over Q4 sits at the 77th percentile of its own 10-year history — culture leaders are not historically cheap on this measure; the premium has held up even as returns stalled. (3) The era-swap test shows the late-era weights work in both periods (+8.8pp early, +11.7pp late) while early-era weights stopped working (+13.3pp → -0.3pp): the culture–performance link did not vanish, but which dimensions carry it changed.

Conventions & caveats

  • Point-in-time EPS: a quarterly figure counts at snapshot T only if its filing date ≤ T (missing filing dates: period end + 75 days). TTM = 4 most recent reported quarters, latest within 380 days of T, span ≤ 400 days.
  • Annual-only reporters: 0 tickers in the backtest universe report only annually; the TTM rule (4 quarters within 400 days) excludes them from EPS metrics by construction, and they are flagged in fund_summary.json.
  • Split convention identical to the variant study: formation snapshots before 2020-12-31 vs after.
  • Reported diluted EPS is unadjusted for later splits; medians are robust to the few affected company-years, and the valuation analysis uses market-cap-based E/P which is split-proof.
  • Return decomposition uses portfolio medians; the gap to the actual equal-weight price return reflects buybacks/issuance, composition and median-vs-mean effects.
  • Era-swap weights are look-ahead by construction (both vectors use future information at early snapshots); it is a diagnostic, not a tradable strategy. Same survivorship caveats as the backtest.
  • Bootstrap SDs: 200 resamples per window, global model, stored ridge alpha.
